decisions.reason: The address autocomplete web service is a low-cost extension of the firm's existing data infrastructure that supports its move to standardized data exchange, so it meets a modest aspiration and the firm's growth leaves enough slack to carry it.

The Austrian gas grid fee database draws on the firm's core database know-how in an adjacent market, and although its demand is less certain, an expanding firm has the slack to keep it rather than start problemistic search.
Peak load window determination is a regulatory calculation that network operators must perform, so it fits the firm's compliance-service core and is likely to meet aspirations.
The end-customer tariff database is a multi-model line close to the firm's market data business and has steady demand from suppliers, so there is no shortfall to trigger dropping it.
Custom web services are a flexible offering that matches the platform and SaaS strategy and costs little to maintain, so keeping it is consistent with satisficing behaviour.
The postal code lookup service is a cheap data utility tied to the firm's address and grid databases, so it is plausibly kept unless it is quietly bundled into another service.
